literature: Fischer 1984: 45; Lane 1982: 81, 84 (photos); Langwill 1980: 30; Plenckers 1970: 58, 85 (photo); Lane 1982: 81, 84 (photos); SmithD 1989: 30; Carter 2012: 204 (photos), 206-07; Amsterdam, Rijksmuseum, website (photo).
remarks: The only pre-1800 trombone by a French maker known to survive. Two plain flat slide-stays, contoured in shape, with two screws fastening upper plates to lower plate serve as an indication of resconstruction at a later date, since screws of this type were unknown in the sixteenth century. Lever, 183mm long, attached to moveable slide-stay. Ferrules have mushroom-like patten in center fields. Bell-stay is a thin piece of metal, square in cross-section, 3.5mm wide, fastened by pins to neck-pipe on one side and bell-pipe on the other. Dents in bell. Signature on hatched background. The instrument’s sounding length is too short to serve as a Quartbass, pitched a fourth below the tenor instrument, and it lacks the additional coil of tubing in the bell section customarily found on bass trombones from this period. If its present condition represents its original state, it may have been constructed as a Terz-Posaun, pitched a third below the tenor instrument. Examined by Carter, August 2000.
